title: How Stonehenge Was Built Without Metal Tools
description: Giant sarsens, Welsh bluestones and sunrise alignments, around 2500 BCE.

scenes.narration: Some of these stones weigh around twenty-five tonnes, and the builders had no metal tools.
scenes.image_prompt: huge sarsen stone being raised by Neolithic people with ropes and timber, Stonehenge

scenes.narration: It's around 2500 BCE, on Salisbury Plain in England.
scenes.image_prompt: rolling green Salisbury Plain with a half-built stone circle, Neolithic people, cloudy sky

scenes.narration: Giant sarsen stones are dragged from about twenty-five kilometres away.
scenes.image_prompt: Neolithic people dragging a giant stone on a wooden sledge over log rails

scenes.narration: Smaller bluestones came from Wales, around 225 kilometres away.
scenes.image_prompt: Neolithic people moving a blue-grey stone through Welsh hills

scenes.narration: Workers shape the stones with stone hammers and join them like woodwork.
scenes.image_prompt: Neolithic workers pounding a stone with round hammerstones, shaping a joint

scenes.narration: The stones line up with sunrise at midsummer and sunset at midwinter.
scenes.image_prompt: sunrise shining through the stones of Stonehenge on midsummer morning

scenes.narration: Crowds gather nearby for great feasts. Pig bones suggest midwinter celebrations.
scenes.image_prompt: Neolithic winter feast with fires and roasting pigs near a stone circle

scenes.narration: Nobody knows exactly why it was built. What's your theory?
scenes.image_prompt: Stonehenge today at dramatic sunset with clouds
